conventions.convention: The dual W-action is contragredient. Reflection vectors satisfy sx=x−α_s∨(x)α_s; their product α_s(y)α_s∨(x) is independent of rescaling.
The mixed commutator is [y,x]=t x(y)−Σ_s c_s α_s(y)α_s∨(x)s, with [a,b]=ab−ba. Category O uses t=1; the rank-one order-two relation is [y,x]=1−2cs.

The notation C[h*] denotes S(h*). Category-O objects are finite over this polynomial subalgebra, and every vector is killed by all sufficiently high total-degree elements of S(h). Standards induce finite-dimensional W-modules with h acting by zero.

KZ uses horizontal sections of the left differential-module connection. The generator s_H has conormal eigenvalue ζ_H; a positive meridian lifts through angle 2π/e_H to the s_H⁻¹ translate, with endpoint identification s_H. Its prescribed roots are ζ_H^j exp(−2πi r_H,j/e_H), including μ_H,0=1.
The highest-weight order is E<F when a_E−a_F is a positive integer; generalized standards truncate Y in degrees greater than n, retaining degrees 0 through n.
The final equivalence concerns the Serre quotient by objects with zero localization and assumes dim_C H_q(c)(W)=|W| explicitly.

load_bearing.statement: For every stated reflection datum, parameter c and t∈C, the ordered monomials x₁^a₁⋯xₙ^aₙ w y₁^b₁⋯yₙ^bₙ form a complex-vector-space basis of H_t,c.

For every finite complex reflection group and every parameter, category O has a finite projective generator that is a direct summand of G_n,c for sufficiently large n; it is equivalent to finite-dimensional modules over a finite-dimensional algebra, and projective covers have standard filtrations with the stated highest-weight order.

The displayed Dunkl assignment is injective and becomes an isomorphism after inverting δ. Every localized category-O object is a finite locally free module with integrable W-equivariant connection; localization followed by fiber monodromy is exact.

For every n≥0, localized G_n,c has connection matrices polynomial in c and holomorphic monodromy matrices; the exact defining Hecke meridian polynomials annihilate its KZ fiber at every parameter, and consequently annihilate KZ(M) for every M∈O_c.

Localization identifies O_c/T fully faithfully with a full subcategory of algebraic W-equivariant bundles with integrable connection; monodromy on this subcategory is fully faithful and its essential image is closed under subobjects and quotients, for every parameter and finite complex reflection group.

The Euler-locally-finite coinduced costandard ∇_c(E) belongs to O_c, has socle L(E) once, satisfies Hom(Δ(E),∇(F))=δ_EF C and Ext¹(Δ(E),∇(F))=0, and has the same K₀ class as Δ(E), without a real-reflection or self-duality assumption.

For irreducible E,F, (P(E):Δ(F))=[∇(F):L(E)]=[Δ(F):L(E)]. With r_E=dim KZ(L(E)), P_KZ=⊕_E P(E)^r_E represents the exact vector-space-valued KZ functor and dim End_O(P_KZ)=|W|, without a Hecke-rank hypothesis.

concerns.concern: The Etingof–Ma source locator describes “§§5.1–5.2, Dunkl localization and the KZ connection”. In the linked text, those sections concern the geometric approach and completion; Dunkl localization is §3.4 and KZ is §6.2. The local proof supplies the argument, but this source locator misdirects the reader. Checked against the section headings in https://arxiv.org/pdf/1001.0432.

alerts.finding: Published thm-laurent-coefficient-formula-and-uniqueness, proof step 2.1, says “therefore every finite sum equals” 2πi c_n. The truncated sum ranges over −N≤k≤N, so this equality requires N≥|n|. For example, f(z)=z, a=0, n=1 and N=0 give zero for the truncated integral although c_1=1. The eventual equality suffices for the limit argument; the word “every” lacks this index qualification.
